title: Queue aggregation hang and fairness remediation
creator: Priya Desai
description: Summary: During a week of elevated load (2026-02-08 to 2026-02-09) we observed sustained tail-latency regressions and request pileups on a subset of serving shards. Symptoms included: stalled queue aggregation (coalescer) on GPU shards, skewed token assignment leading to long-lived slots, and uneven request throughput between tenants. This ticket tracks the incident analysis, short-term mitigations that were applied, and the long-term remediation plan to prevent recurrence.
timeline:
2026-02-08 04:10 UTC: Alert fired - 99th percentile latency > 2x baseline for region-us-west-2; 04:12: ops notified.
2026-02-08 04:18 UTC: On-call observed increasing queue depth on 8/24 shards and matching CPU/IO contention spikes.
2026-02-08 04:25 UTC: Emergency throttle to soft-rate-limit non-enterprise tenants applied (rollback path in place).
2026-02-08 04:40 UTC: Deployed temporary coalescer bypass to force per-request forwarding for affected shards (reduced pileups but increased avg cost).
2026-02-08 05:30 UTC: Root cause hypothesis formed: coalescer state machine entered a starvation path when slot-timeouts and KV-cache-evictions aligned under high variance request sizes.
2026-02-09 to 2026-02-25: Investigation and repro infra created; load tests run to replicate behavior; initial fixes prototyped.
2026-03-05: Canary rollout of revised slot allocator + backpressure heuristics started for 10% of serving fleet.
2026-03-12: Canary metrics look good; promoting fixes to broader fleet pending additional telemetry retention and a follow-up safety rollout plan.
root_cause: Combination of three interacting factors: (1) coalescer queue aggregation state machine allowed indefinite coalescing when certain percentile mixtures of short/long requests arrived, (2) KV cache eviction bursts increased request processing variance and delayed completions for long-lived slots, and (3) global concurrency limiter thresholds were too permissive for the observed variance, allowing shards to accumulate uneven work. The interplay produced lottery-like slot ownership where some tenants experienced starvation and others monopolized GPU slots, producing tail latency spikes.
mitigations: Immediate: Applied soft-rate-limits and temporarily bypassed aggregation on affected shards to drain queues (rollbackable).
Short-term: Implemented a slot-age timeout that forces a flush after N ms of aggregation to bound stall duration.
Short-term: Introduced token-count based admission gate to prevent very long requests from starving the aggregation window.
Medium-term: Adjusted KV cache eviction pacing to avoid synchronized eviction bursts across worker processes.
Long-term: Rewired coalescer state machine to an explicit lease model (slot leases with preemption and graceful handoff) and added per-tenant fairness accounting.
Observability: Added a dedicated dashboard tracking coalescer queue length, slot age distribution, and per-shard fairness ratios.
